# Amaquet Documentation

> Official documentation for Amaquet, a standalone typed in-memory database written in Go with its own binary protocol, persistence layer, Go client, and HTTP administration API.

Use these implementation-aligned pages for installation, protocol integration, data-type behavior, operations, and development. The complete documentation is also available as one machine-readable file at `/llms-full.txt`.

## Complete export

- [Amaquet documentation — full text](/llms-full.txt): Complete Markdown content for every published documentation page in a single file.

## Core documentation

- [Amaquet documentation](/): Official Amaquet documentation for installing, configuring, operating, and integrating with the standalone typed in-memory database and its binary protocol.
- [Amaquet architecture](/architecture/): Amaquet architecture reference covering the sharded storage engine, typed values, protocol server, Go client, HTTP control plane, and append-only persistence.
- [Amaquet protocol specification v1](/protocol/): Amaquet protocol v1 reference for connection URIs, binary frames, multiplexing, negotiation, authentication, commands, Pub/Sub events, and RBAC.

## Getting started

- [Configuration](/getting-started/configuration/): Configure Amaquet listeners, authentication, TLS, persistence, memory limits, request admission, and compression for local or production deployments.
- [Installation](/getting-started/installation/): Install Amaquet from source, configure its server and CLI binaries, secure the first startup, and verify an authenticated request.
- [Quick start](/getting-started/quickstart/): Run Amaquet locally, create a first key, connect with amaquet-cli, and move from an unauthenticated example to a secure deployment.

## Concepts

- [Architecture](/concepts/architecture/): Amaquet separates protocol, authorization, dispatch, storage, value implementations, persistence, and administration.
- [Adaptive in-memory compression](/concepts/compression/): Amaquet can store selected large values in compressed form while preserving their normal Amaquet data type.
- [Engine internals](/concepts/engine-internals/): This page describes the behavior implemented by internal/core, including constraints that are not visible in the short command reference.
- [Keyspace and lifecycle](/concepts/keyspace/): This page explains how Amaquet stores keys, applies expiration, and performs conditional lifecycle operations.
- [Memory and concurrency model](/concepts/memory-model/): This page explains entry metadata, shard-level concurrency, object-level synchronization, and transaction locking.
- [Persistence and recovery](/concepts/persistence/): Amaquet keeps the active data set in its own in-memory engine. Optional persistence uses the Amaquet append-only write-ahead journal (AOF); it does not depend…
- [Security model](/concepts/security/): Amaquet separates transport security, machine credentials, human member identities, HTTP cookie sessions, RBAC, and optional server identity.
- [Why Amaquet?](/concepts/why-amaquet/): Compare Amaquet and Redis across protocol compatibility, typed data models, concurrency, persistence, security, operations, and deployment fit.

## Protocol

- [Amaquet authentication and identity](/protocol/authentication/): This page describes protocol negotiation, API-key authentication, permissions, and optional Ed25519 identity verification.
- [Command reference](/protocol/commands/): Complete reference for Amaquet top-level commands, arguments, validation rules, result shapes, conditional writes, scans, batches, and chunked binary transfers.
- [Binary framing](/protocol/framing/): Every Amaquet frame has a fixed 24-byte header followed by a bounded payload.
- [Amaquet protocol overview](/protocol/overview/): Amaquet is Amaquet's binary framed protocol. It is not RESP and it does not proxy Redis.
- [Connection URIs](/protocol/uri/): Use Amaquet connection URIs to select a protocol transport and identify the target server endpoint.
- [Wire values and snapshots](/protocol/wire-values/): The type string must be one of the names returned by TYPES. Unknown names and malformed representations are rejected before mutation.

## Data types

- [Data types](/data-types/): Browse Amaquet's 91 stable wire-level data types, their categories, construction commands, supported operations, and links to detailed references.
- [Bit structures](/data-types/bit-structures/): Bit structures provide compact bit-level and integer-set storage.
- [Collections](/data-types/collections/): Collections are synchronized mutable structures manipulated with OP.
- [Geospatial](/data-types/geospatial/): Geospatial types use latitude/longitude coordinates and spatial predicates.
- [Graph, synchronization, and network](/data-types/graph-synchronization-and-network/): These types cover graph adjacency, atomic coordination, synchronization, rate limiting, and network values.
- [Indexes and search](/data-types/indexes-and-search/): Index/search types provide exact, range, prefix, full-text, vector, and secondary lookup paths.
- [Type construction and operation reference](/data-types/operations/): Reference the Amaquet protocol contract for constructing and operating on typed values, including arguments, defaults, results, persistence, and failures.
- [Probabilistic](/data-types/probabilistic/): Probabilistic structures provide bounded-memory estimates and membership/frequency queries.
- [Queues and messaging](/data-types/queues-and-messaging/): Queue and messaging types provide ordering, delivery, streaming, and publication semantics.
- [Scalar](/data-types/scalar/): Scalar values are stored directly in a key and use SET.
- [Structured](/data-types/structured/): Structured values cover documents, encoded payloads, records, matrices, and tensors.
- [Time series](/data-types/time-series/): Time-series types store timestamped numeric data and derived statistics.
- [Vectors](/data-types/vectors/): Vector types support embeddings, metadata, quantization, and similarity search.

## Operations

- [Backup and recovery](/operations/backups/): This page explains which Amaquet state must be protected and how to create, validate, and restore recovery artifacts.
- [Capacity planning](/operations/capacity/): Amaquet keeps the active database in memory. Plan capacity from the stored data, indexes, Go object overhead, protocol buffers, temporary work space,…
- [Production deployment](/operations/deployment/): Use this guidance to deploy Amaquet as a secure, monitored single-node stateful service.
- [Docker](/operations/docker/): The repository contains Dockerfile, a loopback-only development docker-compose.yml, and a TLS-oriented docker-compose.production.yml.
- [Observability](/operations/observability/): This page describes the native and HTTP surfaces that expose Amaquet health, capacity, and runtime metrics.
- [Production hardening](/operations/production-hardening/): Amaquet applies bounded-resource, fail-stop, and revocation rules for a single-node production deployment.
- [TLS and protocol identity](/operations/tls/): Configure TLS for transport security and optional Ed25519 keys for stable application-level server identity.
- [Troubleshooting](/operations/troubleshooting/): Use these symptoms and corrective actions to diagnose common startup, authentication, persistence, TLS, and test failures.

## Development

- [Adding a data type](/development/adding-types/): A new stable type touches several contracts. Keep them synchronized.
- [Development build](/development/build/): Use these commands and Make targets to build, test, and serve Amaquet and its documentation during development.
- [Developer workflow fuzzing](/development/developer-fuzzing/): Amaquet has a second black-box fuzz layer in addition to the 91 per-type fuzzers.
- [Repository layout](/development/repository-layout/): This diagram maps the repository's executable, implementation, client, automation, test, and documentation directories.
- [Bash testing and fuzzing](/development/testing-fuzzing/): Amaquet includes a black-box Bash contract and a mutation-fuzz entrypoint for every stable wire data type.

## Reference

- [Administration API](/reference/admin-api/): Operate Amaquet through its HTTP administration API for authentication, organizations, members, API keys, RBAC, data access, metrics, and audit events.
- [CLI reference](/reference/cli/): Use the Amaquet command-line tools for native protocol commands, API-key authentication, server identity generation, and verified checkpoint restoration.
- [Configuration reference](/reference/configuration/): Reference every Amaquet JSON configuration field, including defaults, accepted values, validation rules, security implications, and operational effects.
- [Error model](/reference/errors/): Amaquet response errors include a stable code and human-readable message.
- [Glossary](/reference/glossary/): AOF — Append-only file containing journaled Amaquet mutation requests.
- [Go client library](/reference/go-client/): Integrate Amaquet from Go with the concurrent-safe client, TCP or TLS dialing, request multiplexing, authentication, subscriptions, and typed commands.
- [Implementation coverage map](/reference/implementation-coverage/): This page maps the production repository to the documentation that describes it.
